**Premise correction:** There is no nightly database-cleanup job scheduled anywhere in this repository. The codebase does contain a cron-style scheduler package, `internal/scheduler` (with a `ParseCronExpression`/`Schedule` cron parser in `internal/scheduler/parser.go` and a `Scheduler` type in `internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`), but it is entirely unused in production: a repo-wide search shows `internal/scheduler` is imported only by its own test files (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go` and `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go`) — no server code, `cmd/`, or background runner ever imports or registers a job with it.

The only actual scheduled background work in the server is the two runners wired up in `server/server.go` (`startBackgroundRunners`, `server/server.go:153-174`): the S3 presign runner (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`, every 12 hours) and the (unused-in-production) memo-payload rebuild runner — neither of which does database cleanup, and neither of which uses the `internal/scheduler` cron package or runs at a specific "nightly" clock time; the S3 presign runner uses a plain `time.Ticker` interval, not a cron schedule.

**Actual mechanism:** None exists — there is no nightly cleanup job to report a scheduled time for.
